summary: The learning map is drawn as a graph with arrows (route-graph.js: layering by longest prerequisite chain, lanes for long arrows, crossing reduction, placement under prerequisites) with a detail panel that names what a concept needs, what it opens and, for a locked one, which prerequisites it is waiting for; no layer numbers on pages or recommendation cards. The AI prompt now asks for a dependency graph (independent entry points, 2-3 prerequisites, no chain) and the page says so when a draft is a single line. Big maps stay inside a scrollable, zoomable viewport; the creation page stacks graph over detail. Projects can be renamed and deleted (project.html, type-the-name confirmation, database backup first, newest 3 kept; explicit ids only). Existing projects can ask for an AI draft of the map from the map page through a NEW operation learning_path_plan_project that is registered with owner_approved false, so the gateway refuses it until the owner approves; the learning_path_plan instruction share was rebalanced 500->560 and framing 150->90 inside the unchanged 1200 cap.
scope_note: Branch feature/route-mode on top of ec7a6e0. Changes the budget registry (new unapproved operation, instruction share) and a prompt: critical by path. The owner's .claude files are excluded locally.

budget_impact.rationale: No model call is made by default or by this change. The new learning_path_plan_project operation is registered with owner_approved false and the gateway refuses it before sending until the owner changes that flag; when approved its cap is the same as learning_path_plan (input 1200, output 900, about $0.00111 reference and $0.00144 cap per call, arithmetic estimates from scripts/budget.py, not measurements). The prompt text is new and has never been sent to a model.
budget_impact.before: Existing projects had no way to get a learning map except by hand; the instruction share was 500 with a 150 margin.
budget_impact.after: One more registered, unapproved interactive operation; instruction share 560 and margin 90 for learning_path_plan (cap unchanged).
budget_impact.developer_usage: unknown; host does not expose complete aggregate developer token accounting

additional_checks.scope: PaperDigHelper.app rebuilt; window not clicked through

reviews.reviewer: One separate read-only code-review agent (same model family, not a human); findings fixed afterwards, fixes not re-read by a reviewer.

open_risks: No real model call: whether the new prompt yields branched maps is unmeasured; the single-line warning exists because it may not.

learning_path_plan_project is NOT approved. The owner must set owner_approved to true in harness/budget.json (or say so) before an existing project can use the AI draft; until then the page says it is waiting for approval.
The independent review was by an agent of the same model family; its findings were fixed and the fixes were not re-read by a reviewer.
route-page.js, project-page.js and the mount() half of route-graph.js have no automated DOM tests; they were checked by hand in a browser preview. The static contract tests are mostly source greps.
A half-typed concept edit is lost when leaving the page; deleting a project during an in-flight plan call recreates a harmless counter row.

Not exercised: the Tauri window, dark mode, keyboard-only use. Not done: knowledge-base (Cytoscape) path layer, profile-page Route Mode block, growing the map (slice 7), governance documents (slice 8).
Project keywords are not editable from the new page (they are the profile's pinned terms).
